task:
Bug, real and observed on 2026-09-16: the 10:00 job-search run fired TWICE, about 63 seconds apart. Two digest emails went out - the first reporting 0 new / 0 shortlisted, the second the real 160 new / 1 shortlisted. She received both. NEEDS THIS MACHINE - launchd registration is machine-local state, not something the repo tracks.

Investigate:
- launchctl list | grep -i mobyai
- Inspect scripts/com.mobyai.jobsearch.plist in the repo AND whatever is actually loaded under ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ - they can differ. Look for a duplicate StartCalendarInterval entry, two different labels pointing at the same script, or the job having been bootstrapped twice.

Fix by removing/unloading the duplicate registration. Do NOT fix this by editing the pipeline code or adding a lock file - the pipeline is behaving correctly, it is being invoked twice.

Two honest caveats worth holding onto:
- The 0 new / 0 shortlisted first email is a real clue. A plain duplicate registration would more likely produce two similar-looking runs, not one empty one. An empty first run then a full second run also fits "first invocation raced ahead of something it needed" - a stale dist/, a source not yet reachable, a cold cache.
- So if the evidence does not actually support the duplicate-registration theory, say so plainly and report what you did find instead. Do not force the theory to fit.

Report what was registered before and after, and which explanation the evidence actually supports.

macmini.output:
Investigated thoroughly; the duplicate-registration theory is NOT supported by the evidence. Reporting what I actually found instead, per the task's own instruction.

Registered before: launchctl list showed exactly one label (com.mobyai.jobsearch). The repo's scripts/com.mobyai.jobsearch.plist and the installed ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.mobyai.jobsearch.plist differ only in REPO_PATH substitution (installed points at /Users/irtizaahmed/AI-Agent-System.worktrees/jobsearch-pipeline, a dedicated worktree set up for this pipeline) - no duplicate StartCalendarInterval entries, no second label.

Checked macOS's own unified log (log show, last 24h) for actual launchd firing events for this label - the authoritative source, independent of the app's own logs: exactly ONE 'Registered StartCalendarInterval' event at 00:22:13 (5 weekday entries, all at 11:00, IDs 268435470-474) and exactly ONE 'Running StartCalendarInterval' firing today, at 11:00:04, immediately rescheduled for next Wednesday, service went inactive at 11:01:14 (~70s runtime). No second firing exists anywhere in the log. The pipeline's own cost ledger (logs/costs.jsonl) has exactly one entry today, timestamped 11:01:08 - consistent with one run, not two.

What actually produced two emails: --all runs every profile from listProfiles(), which returns directory names alphabetically sorted - irtiza before shivani. DIGEST_EMAIL_TO is a single global env var, not scoped per profile, so BOTH profiles' digests get emailed to the same address in the same run. Today's single 11:00 run did exactly that: irtiza's digest first (0 new/0 shortlisted - its one source is currently broken, HTTP 503, so it resolves near-instantly), then shivani's real digest ~60-70s later (160 new). That is almost certainly the 'two emails, 63 seconds apart, first empty then real' Irtiza described - not a duplicate firing of the same digest, but two different profiles' legitimate digests landing in the same inbox back to back. The task described this as happening at '10:00'; the plist's own schedule was 10:00 on the pre-merge branch and is 11:00 as of today's merged main - I can't confirm what time it fired on whatever day the incident was actually observed, but the same 'shared recipient across profiles' mechanism applies regardless of the hour.

No fix applied, per the task's own instruction (no pipeline code edit, no lock file) - there is nothing here that a lock file would fix, since it's not a race, it's two correct sequential emails to one recipient. Worth a separate decision from Irtiza (not actioned by me, just flagging): whether irtiza's own job-search digest should go to a different address than Shivani's, since right now his results land in her inbox too. Leaving that as a new observation, not something I changed.
